editorial:
Imagine being a kid and suddenly feeling like you have a direct line to the creator of the universe. That is exactly what you get with this unique story. You follow a young boy who is struggling to figure out who he is and where he fits in. It feels like a mix of a family drama and a weird dream, but it never gets too heavy. The vibe is very soft and thoughtful, focusing more on the inner world of a child than on a big, loud plot. It is the kind of movie that makes you stop and think about your own childhood and the questions you used to ask about how the world works.

What really works here is the lead actor, who makes the boy's confusion feel totally real. The pacing is a bit slow, so if you want explosions or fast twists, this isn't for you. However, if you like quiet stories that tug at your heart, you will love it. You can easily find this to rent on Apple TV or stream it on Prime Video. If you are a fan of high-quality home cinema, adding the 4K Blu-ray to your physical collection is a great move since the colors and scenery look beautiful in high definition.
endingExplained: In the end, the boy realizes that his conversations with God were actually a way for him to deal with his own loneliness and growing pains. There is no big supernatural reveal or magic trick. Instead, he finds peace with his identity and learns to accept himself as he is. The movie wraps up with a sweet moment of clarity where he stops searching for answers outside himself and starts feeling happy in his own skin.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves gentle stories about growing up and finding yourself.
